note: The Bulgarian National Bank's Ordinance No. 22 on the Central Credit Register, articles 10(3) and 20: lenders report the state of every active credit monthly, as at the month's last day, with no threshold, written as 30 days; the monthly data is kept five years from the period it covers. bnb.bg answered with its web firewall's refusal, so the ordinance was read in Kik-Info's legal database. Re-read 2026-11-03: the BNB's own English text of the ordinance (consolidated to DV 113/2025, read in Common Crawl's capture of bnb.bg of 16 October 2026) states articles 10(3) and 20 as Kik-Info gives them, so the fact is found on the primary and Kik-Info's copy is no longer cited. Article 10(2), as amended from 1 February 2026, also has a new or amended loan agreement reported within two business days; the monthly report of each loan's state is what the 30 days read.

sources.title: Bulgarian National Bank, Ordinance No 22 of 16 July 2009 on the Central Credit Register (BNB's English text, consolidated to Darjaven Vestnik issue 113 of 2025, effective 1 January 2026); read in Common Crawl's capture CC-MAIN-2026-43 of 16 October 2026 (file Last-Modified 25 September 2026)
sources.said: Article 10. ... (3) ... Institutions and entities under Article 4, paragraph 1 shall provide by the fifteenth day of the month following the reporting period information on the state of all active loans of their customers by the last day of the reporting month. ... Article 20. ... The monthly information on loans provided by institutions and entities under Article 4, paragraph 1 shall be stored in the Central Credit Register for a term of five years from the reporting period the information refers to.
